summary: Vietnam issues its eVisa to citizens of all countries and territories — 25 USD single entry or 50 USD multiple entry, valid up to 90 days — while around two dozen nationalities, including several EU countries, Japan and South Korea, enter visa-free for up to 45 days.

fee.notes: Paid online by card; the fee is non-refundable even if the application is refused. Open to citizens of all countries and territories.
Paid online by card; the fee is non-refundable even if the application is refused. Open to citizens of all countries and territories.
Base stamping fee for a single-entry visa; total cost and service charges vary by embassy. Confirm with the mission where you apply.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on the date of arrival.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required only if you arrive from, or transited through, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not currently an entry requirement for tourists, but medical coverage is strongly recommended — good private hospitals are expensive.

onwardTicket.text: Airlines and immigration officers may ask visa-exempt and eVisa travelers for proof of onward or return travel within the permitted stay.

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published, but officers may ask about means of support for the stay.

currencyLimits.text: Cash over 5,000 USD (or equivalent foreign currency) or over 15,000,000 VND must be declared to customs on arrival and departure.

notes: Duty-free allowance: 200 cigarettes and 1.5 liters of spirits (or 2 liters of alcohol under 20%) per adult.
No arrival card is required; customs declaration forms are needed only if you carry declarable goods or cash.

payments.text: Cards work in hotels, malls and upscale restaurants, but street food, markets, taxis and most small businesses are cash-first. Local QR payments are booming but generally need a Vietnamese bank account.

safety.text: Vietnam is generally safe for visitors with low violent crime. Watch for petty theft, bag-snatching from motorbikes in big cities, and chaotic traffic.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Vietnam Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: Vietnam spans several climate zones: roughly November to April is driest in the south, while the north is best from October to April; central beaches shine from February to July.

idp.text: Vietnam is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either.

driving.text: Vietnam is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Vietnam yet.

tips.text: Apply for the eVisa only at the official portal (evisa.gov.vn / evisa.xuatnhapcanh.gov.vn). Lookalike sites charge 50–100 USD "service fees" for the same 25 USD visa or deliver nothing.
Your eVisa is checked character by character: passport number, name spelling and date of birth must match exactly, and you must enter through the checkpoint selected in the application.
Traffic is the biggest practical risk. If you rent a motorbike you need a valid license with motorcycle category recognized in Vietnam — many travel insurance policies refuse claims without one.
Carry cash for daily spending and count zeros carefully — 500,000 and 20,000 VND notes are both blue and easy to confuse.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Vietnam?
faq.answer: Yes. US passport holders need a visa; the easiest route is the official eVisa — 25 USD single entry or 50 USD multiple entry, valid up to 90 days — applied for at evisa.gov.vn (evisa.xuatnhapcanh.gov.vn). Processing normally takes about 3 business days.

faq.question: Which nationalities can enter Vietnam without a visa?
faq.answer: Around two dozen nationalities enter visa-free, including citizens of the UK, Germany, France, Italy and Spain (45 days, unilateral exemption extended through 2028), Japan, South Korea and Russia (45 days), and ASEAN neighbors (Philippines 21 days, Indonesia and most others 30 days).

faq.question: How much does the Vietnam eVisa cost and how long does it take?
faq.answer: The eVisa costs 25 USD for single entry or 50 USD for multiple entry, allows a stay of up to 90 days, and is normally processed in about 3 business days (longer around Vietnamese holidays). It is available to citizens of all countries.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Vietnam?
faq.answer: There is no routine tourist extension: eVisas are generally not extendable, so most travelers exit the country and re-enter on a new eVisa. Plan your dates before you apply.

faq.question: Does Vietnam require an arrival card or customs declaration?
faq.answer: No arrival card is required. You only complete a customs declaration if you carry declarable items or cash over 5,000 USD (or 15,000,000 VND).
